topic: Tip: raise the grain before staining
caption:
Water-based stain makes wood fibres stand up, so the surface feels rough after the first coat. Fix it before you stain: wipe the sanded wood with a damp cloth, let it dry fully, then sand lightly with 220 grit. Stain after that and it stays smooth. Swipe for the steps. Do you do this step? topic: Tip: stop blotchy stain on pine
caption:
Pine, birch, maple and poplar take stain unevenly, which is why you get dark patches. Sand evenly, apply a wood conditioner first, wipe off the excess along the grain and test on an offcut from the same piece. Swipe and save this for your next job. topic: Tip: stir your stain, do not shake it
caption:
Shaking a tin of stain puts air bubbles into the finish, and they show up as tiny marks on the wood. Stir slowly from the bottom until the colour is even, and stir again every few minutes while you work, because pigment settles. Same shade from the first piece to the last. Tag a carpenter who still shakes the tin. Need advice? Call us on 63644 44120.
